newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares end just up, Greenspan crushes gains.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares end just up, Greenspan crushes gains.

text.p: Dutch shares just pushed ahead to set a new closing high after the Federal Reserve Chairman's crushed gains made early afternoon, dealers said.

The AEX index of 25 leading stocks ended up just 0.32 points at 750.51, but the light nudge upwards at the death was sufficient to set a new closing high. By mid-afternoon, the AEX had set a new intra-day peak of 755.73 points, before Greenspans's comments upset U.S. and European markets.
U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan said he was upbeat on the U.S. economy, but saw an upside risk on inflation and could not rule out a pre-emptive rate rise.

"Such caution seems especially warranted with regard to the sharp rise in equity prices during the past two years. These gains have obviously raised questions of sustainability," Greenspan said on Wednesday.
The comments immediately sent shares down. The AEX index reached a low of 745.10 points, before they clawing back.
The strength of the Dutch market and the late resilience was the result of a few star turns from companies reporting their full year figures and an impressive rise from Unilever.
Unilever, the largest gainer of the leading 25 stocks, put on 5.60 guilders to end at 375.50 points.
"Unilever is continuing to gain on its restructuring and its positive results," one trader said.
Dutch companies announcing results on Wednesday all offered something positive, providing an extra boost to the market.
Biochemicals and food group Gist Brocade rose by 3.00 guilders to 62.20 after reporting a 10 percent increase in net profits. It said it expected a clear rise in operating profit in 1997.
"The results were in line with expectations, but the outlook is pretty favourable," one trader said.

Trading company Hagemeyer added 2.60 guilders to 165.50 after reporting a 47.5 percent increase in net profit, at the very top end of analysts' expectations, as well as a two-for-one stock split. It added it expected sales to grow to about 11 or 12 billion guilders, from eight billion, in the next few years.
"It's really more than expected, coming with the stock split too," one trader said.
Finally chemicals firm Akzo added 4.90 guilders to 283.10 a day ahead of its full year result announcement.
